Team —

Putting this in one thread so we have a single source of truth for the runbook and training schedule ahead of the Nov launch with Atlas. Attached: readiness_stoplight_v1.xlsx (stoplight by owner), runbook_draft_v0.9.pdf (ops + rollback draft), training_matrix_v1.xlsx (who needs what).

Key asks:
- Owners: review the stoplight and confirm gaps by EOD Mon (11/2). I’ve highlighted high-risk items in red.
- Training: we need two 60-min sessions (overview + ops run-through) for CS, SE, and SRE. Propose Tue 11/4 10:00 and Thu 11/6 15:00 PT.
- Gating: propose go/no-go check at T-24h with the criteria in runbook section 2. Laura — can you confirm the gating checklist?
- Rollback: please validate rollback steps in the runbook. Dylan — is the infrastructure rollback script ready?

Notes: Atlas PM is on CC to stay aligned on timing; they’ve requested a staged rollout by region.

I’ll consolidate owners into the stoplight and send a calendar invite once ppl confirm.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole

Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — quick pass from docs/enablement POV.

I skimmed the runbook and stoplight and flagged the following gaps in the sheet (see red comments):
- Runbook section 1.3: missing exact telemetry thresholds for degraded behavior (who documents alert names). Owner: Dylan/SRE.
- Playbooks: no link to the knowledge base pages for common troubleshooting flows (I can create these but need examples).
- Training matrix: CS needs a shorter 20-min cheat-sheet for customer-facing teams. Suggest we produce a one-pager.
- Release notes template: not included; we should standardize the template and responsibility (Product + Marketing).

Action items I can take: draft KB page skeleton and the one-pager cheat-sheet by Mon EOD if owners agree. Also will add doc owners column to the stoplight.

On the rollback doc: I left an inline comment about verifying DB migration idempotency — we can’t rely on a single fast rollback if migrations are in-flight.

-Kimberly

Couple of product/roadmap notes from my side:
- Staged rollout: we should gate feature flag by customer tier and region. Propose 20% of US traffic -> 50% -> 100% across a 48h window (metrics-driven). We need experiments defined (error rate, latency P95, token cost delta).
- Quantization/Perf: for Atlas we’re using the quantized variant; confirm that the perf profile is in the runbook (latency P50/P95 targets). If not, I’ll paste numbers.
- Exceptions: if performance regression > 15% P95 or error rate > 1% for more than 15 minutes, autoswitch to the compatible fallback model and pause rollout. Documented in runbook but needs owner.

I’ll volunteer to be the rollback-owner for the model routing piece and will be available during the rollout window.

Karthik

Thanks all — I reviewed the runbook and proposed stoplight. A few clarifications from a gate/decision perspective:

Go/No-go (T-24h) must include (minimum):
- All red items in the stoplight either resolved or have an owner + mitigation plan.
- Successful dry-run smoke test in staging with no blocking alerts for 60 minutes.
- Docs: KB one-pager and runbook final copy available in Drive (Kimberly to confirm).
- Customer comms: release notes + support play drafted and approved.

Rollback plan: we will use the model routing + infra script + a single DB feature-flag toggle. Karthik: you own the routing rollback; Dylan: you own infra script; I’ll own the go/no-go call and coordinate with Atlas. I’ve created the JIRA epic SUP-1234 and linked the infra tasks — folks, please add sub-tasks and ETA.

I’ll be on-call for the 24h decision window and will convene a quick 15-min stand T-24h to confirm the gate. For now, I’m happy with the staged 20/50/100 plan.

Laura
VP, Product
